notes: Substantively this is a strong RCA: every chain citation checks out against the fixture, siblings were probed by running them, the fix was verified on a scratch copy, and the duplicate-account sibling (worse than the ticket) was surfaced and argued for. The two failures are both prose-form: 55 lint findings (mostly semicolons) and a multi-sentence headline. Eval critique: assertion 6 is phrased as 'missing normalization at write time' while this report frames the root one level up ('no canonical form, enforced on write and read'); a grader could read that either way, so the assertion would be more discriminating if phrased as 'locates the cause in signup/insert storing raw input, not only in find_by_email'. The skim-test assertion bundles two checks (one-sentence headline; section first sentences) that can fail independently; splitting them would give cleaner signal. Nothing checks that the fixture copy was left unmodified (the report claims it and diff confirms, modulo __pycache__ created by running tests), and nothing rewards sibling claims being verified by execution rather than asserted from reading, which is the most expensive thing this run did right. Assertion 1 is trivially satisfied by any non-empty draft.
